name: Receiving, stores and inventory
summary: The mine's warehouse receives every supplier delivery against a purchase order, keeps several thousand spare parts and consumables, and issues them to mechanics, electricians and mining crews around the clock. Warehouse attendants on 14-on/14-off rotation check deliveries against orders in the ERP, put stock away, issue parts against work orders, exchange rotable components, and send parts underground by cage. Discrepancies go to the buyers, and stockouts turn into urgent orders. Errors come from issues not recorded against a work order, parts put in the wrong bin and vague requests, which spoil stock records and job costs and show up as stockouts when a machine is down.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-650 tpd underground mine and its own mill near Wawa in northern Ontario, with 12-hour shifts on 14-on/14-off rotations and a camp.
baseline.notes: A warehouse building with a receiving bay, counter, bulk storage and yard; the ERP inventory module holds the item master and stock.

unit_of_work: one receipt (one supplier delivery) or one stores issue
trigger: A supplier truck arrives with a delivery, or a mechanic or crew asks for parts.
end_state: The receipt is posted and the stock put away or staged for the job, or the parts are issued and charged to a work order (or an urgent order is raised when nothing is on site).

volume.seasonality: Deliveries peak before spring break-up load restrictions and before planned shutdowns; issues follow maintenance work and rise during shutdowns.

evidence.note: Kept from the organisation file: about 500 purchase orders a month and several thousand stores transactions.
The organisation file shows three planned shutdowns a year (mnt-shutdown); the multiplier is the author's estimate.
All five attendants work in this process; duties as in NOC 14401.
Approvals of requisitions and adjustments, stock reviews.
Receiving discrepancies and expediting.
Gate check-in of deliveries.
Time mechanics and crews spend asking for and collecting parts at the counter.

systems.name: Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Gate access, camp booking and gold room access logs
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network

resources.name: Production shaft hoist, skip and cage (loading pocket below 460 m level to dump at 70 m level)

steps.name: Pick up the next job at the warehouse
steps.description: The warehouse attendant on shift takes the next piece of work: a supplier truck at the gate with a delivery, or a mechanic or crew member at the counter, on the phone or on a pick list asking for parts. They decide whether it is a receipt or an issue.

evidence.note: Split assumes about 600 receipts and 1,600 issues a month from the organisation file's 500 purchase orders and 2,200 transactions.

steps.name: Check the delivery truck in at the gate
steps.description: The security officer checks the driver's identity and paperwork at the gatehouse, records the truck in the gate log, gives the site safety rules and radios the warehouse that a delivery is coming.

control.basis: Site access and security procedure: all vehicles logged at the gatehouse

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice at a remote mine with a staffed gatehouse (security officers in the organisation file).

steps.name: Unload the delivery
steps.description: The attendant unloads pallets, crates and long material from the truck with the forklift into the receiving bay or yard and signs the driver's bill of lading, noting any visible damage.

error.defect_description: Damage not noted on the bill of lading, so a later claim against the carrier fails.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Match the packing slip to the purchase order and count
steps.description: The attendant looks up the purchase order in the ERP from the packing slip, counts and inspects each line, and compares part numbers and quantities with what was ordered.

error.defect_description: Quantity or part miscounted, so stock and the supplier invoice disagree.

next.condition: short, over, wrong part, damaged or no purchase order

evidence.note: Receiving and sorting of incoming parts is a core storekeeper duty (NOC 14401); discrepancy share and minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Ask the buyer to sort out the discrepancy
steps.description: The attendant emails the buyer with photos and the packing slip; the buyer calls the supplier, agrees a credit, a replacement or a return, or raises a missing purchase order, and tells the warehouse what to do with the goods.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Post the goods receipt in the ERP
steps.description: The attendant enters the received quantities against the purchase order lines in the ERP, which updates stock on hand and makes the receipt available for three-way matching in accounts payable.

error.defect_description: Receipt posted to the wrong line or not posted, so the invoice is held.

control.basis: Internal control over purchasing: goods receipt posted by stores, separate from the buyer and accounts payable, for three-way match

evidence.note: Keeping records of stock on hand is a storekeeper duty (NOC 14401); three-way matching is the author's description of common ERP practice.

steps.name: Label and put away the stock
steps.description: The attendant labels each item with its stock number and bin location and puts it away on the shelves, in the bulk storage or the yard, using the forklift for heavy items.

error.defect_description: Item put in the wrong bin, so it shows in stock but cannot be found.

evidence.note: Storing items in an orderly and accessible manner is a storekeeper duty (NOC 14401); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Stage the direct-charge item and notify the requester
steps.description: The attendant puts the item on the hold shelf tagged with the work order or job, and calls or emails the planner or supervisor who ordered it to collect it or have it sent to the shop.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Ask for parts at the counter
steps.description: A mechanic or crew member comes to the counter with a work order number or a pick list from the planner, or phones from underground, and describes the parts needed, often by machine model and description rather than part number.

evidence.note: Mechanics are the main warehouse customers at a mine (organisation file triggers from maintenance processes); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Look up the part and its stock
steps.description: The attendant searches the ERP item master by part number, description or machine, checks the quantity on hand and bin location, and checks interchangeable numbers when the first one is not found.

error.defect_description: Wrong part identified from a vague description.

next.condition: system shows stock but the bin is empty

evidence.note: Stockout share near the 7.4% industry average stockout rate and the 94.6% inventory accuracy reported by the MMH article; the split between stockout and record error is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Pick the parts
steps.description: The attendant walks to the bins or the yard, picks the quantity, checks it against the request with the mechanic, and brings heavy items with the forklift.

evidence.note: Issuing parts for internal use is a storekeeper duty (NOC 14401); minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the issue against the work order
steps.description: The attendant enters the issue in the ERP against the work order or cost centre and the equipment number, prints or signs the issue slip, and hands over the parts. On night shift or when the counter is busy, issues are written on paper and keyed in later.

error.defect_description: Issue charged to the wrong work order or not keyed in, so stock and job costs are wrong.

control.basis: Inventory control: every stores issue recorded against a work order or cost centre

next.condition: parts handed over at the counter
issue takes the item below its reorder point

evidence.note: Organisation file notes unrecorded issues spoil inventory accuracy; shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Exchange a rotable component
steps.description: For a rotable part (a pump, starter, hydraulic cylinder or transmission) the attendant takes the failed core from the mechanic, tags it for rebuild with the work order, and issues a rebuilt unit from stock.

evidence.note: Organisation file lists rebuilt components flowing back to stores; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Look for a substitute or another source
steps.description: With the planner or the mechanic the attendant checks alternative part numbers, a cannibalized unit, or parts on an order that has arrived but not been received, before raising an urgent order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Raise an urgent requisition
steps.description: The attendant raises a rush purchase requisition in the ERP with the work order and equipment down, and phones the buyer to expedite with the supplier and a hot-shot courier.

next.condition: requisition raised; issue completes when the order arrives

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the parts underground
steps.description: The attendant packs the parts in a tote or on a pallet tagged with the level and work order, books space on the next material cage or personnel-carrier run, and radios the underground crew when they are on their way.

evidence.note: Material moves by cage or ramp between shift changes; wait and minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Raise a replenishment requisition
steps.description: When the ERP shows the item below its reorder point, the attendant reviews usage and raises a replenishment requisition for the reorder quantity.

evidence.note: Preparing requisitions to replenish stock is a storekeeper duty (NOC 14401); the daily batch is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the replenishment requisition
steps.description: The supply chain supervisor reviews the day's replenishment requisitions in the ERP for quantity and value, adjusts reorder points for slow movers, and releases them to the buyers.

control.basis: Purchasing authority limits: requisitions approved by the supply chain supervisor before purchase

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Count the bin and adjust the stock record
steps.description: The attendant counts the bin and nearby locations, searches for the item, checks recent issues and receipts, and prepares a stock adjustment in the ERP with the reason.

evidence.note: Inventory accuracy near 95% means about one lookup in twenty finds a record error; minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve the stock adjustment
steps.description: The supply chain supervisor reviews the adjustment and its value, approves it in the ERP or asks for a recount, and the attendant then treats the item as out of stock.

control.basis: Inventory control: stock adjustments approved by someone other than the person who counted

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Receiving discrepancy
exceptions.description: About 13% of deliveries are short, over, wrong, damaged or arrive without a purchase order; the buyer resolves them with the supplier and about one in five is returned.

exceptions.name: Stockout
exceptions.description: The part is not on site; a substitute is found for about a third, the rest become urgent orders.

exceptions.name: Phantom stock
exceptions.description: The ERP shows stock but the bin is empty, usually after an unrecorded issue or a wrong put-away; the attendant counts, the supervisor approves an adjustment and the request becomes a stockout.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the job reaching the warehouse to receipt posted and put away or parts handed over
benchmarks.population: Mine site warehouse issuing to maintenance around the clock

evidence.note: Counter issues take minutes to an hour including queueing; receipts are usually put away the same or next day.

benchmarks.unit: share of requests not filled from stock (industry average)

evidence.note: Practitioner benchmark, not specific to mining; target 5% or lower.

benchmarks.unit: share of items with correct record (industry average)

evidence.note: Practitioner benchmark, target 95%.

pain_points.description: Parts issued without a slip on night shift or taken underground directly are keyed in late or never, so the ERP shows stock that is not there and job costs are wrong.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description and author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Requests by description rather than part number take repeated searches and lead to wrong parts.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Stockouts of critical spares leave equipment down while urgent orders travel to a remote site.

evidence.note: Industry average stockout rate of 7.4%; the downtime effect is the author's estimate.

sources.title: NOC 2021 unit group 14401: Storekeepers and partspersons
sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada, National Occupational Classification
sources.supports: Storekeepers receive and sort incoming parts and supplies, store them in a warehouse, tool room or supply room, process requisitions and issue parts for internal use, keep records of the amount, kind and location of stock in a manual or computerized inventory system, and prepare requisitions to replenish stock.

sources.title: MRO efficiency can help keep costs down (Phil Hebert and Rick Wakeland)
sources.supports: MRO storeroom key performance indicators: industry average stockouts 7.4% against a target of 5% or lower; inventory accuracy 94.6% against a 95% target; customer service level 95% or higher; inventory turns 2 a year against a target of 4.

assumptions: About 28% of cases are receipts and 72% issues. Cycle time for backorders ends when the urgent requisition is raised; the wait for the supplier belongs to site-purchasing.
Fuel deliveries and underground services materials were added as triggers; the organisation file routes fuel to site-fuel only and lists no stores requests from mine-ug-services.
Mechanics stand in for all requesters at the counter (electricians, millwrights, miners).
The forklift is not in the organisation file and was added as a resource.

The simulated median (about 0.09 days, roughly two hours) is above the 0.05-day estimate because receipts wait for counting and put-away and parts for underground wait for the cage; counter issues alone take under an hour.

The staffing check implies about 11 FTE against 7.3 stated because triangular step times have long tails and requesters' counter time is included; attendants on 14/14 rotation also work about 168 hours a month rather than 130.
Attendants on a 14/14 rotation with 12-hour shifts work about 168 hours a month, more than the 130 productive hours the staffing check assumes.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's rates: base wage times 1.30 for office and staff roles and 1.35 for hourly site roles.
